transcript: Last night I attended a reading of The Laramie Project in commemoration of the 25th anniversary of Matthew Shepherd's death. If you aren't at all familiar with The Laramie Project, you should really read it. It's an essential piece of both theater history and queer history. It chronicles the events of and around the brutal hate crime and murder of Matthew Shepherd in Larry, Wyoming, and the resulting community reactions and criminal trials. As a piece of verbatim theater, it's comprised entirely from otherwise unscripted texts such as interview excerpts, news reports, and court transcripts. Moises Kaufman and Tectonic Theater Project visited Laramie six times and conducted over 200 interviews while creating this piece. Result as a complex and nuanced portrait of community responding to trauma and national media attention. This play was really ahead of its time in so many ways, and this reading was great. Brendon Uranowitz, in particular, was so captivating. On a personal note, I had the pleasure of working with Moise s and tectonic a few years ago and performed in a production of The Larry Project in high school. So last night was like visiting an old friend with that another program for my collection.
